$comment: Curated writing prompts. genre: literary|speculative|horror|mystery|humor|poetry. length: flash|scene|poem. Additions welcome via PR.

prompts.text: A woman returns the library book her mother checked out the week she died. It is nineteen years overdue. Write the conversation at the desk.
Two estranged siblings have to divide their father's tools. Neither of them does the kind of work the tools were for.
Write about the last person to leave a factory on its final day of operation, who is not sad.
A man has been mispronouncing his own surname his entire adult life. Today someone corrects him.
Describe a marriage using only the contents of a refrigerator, across four different years.
Someone practices an apology in the car for twenty minutes. Write what they actually say when the door opens.
A teenager works a summer job at the place their parent was fired from. Nobody at work knows.
Write the moment a lifelong caretaker realizes they are no longer needed, and is relieved.
Two neighbors have not spoken in eleven years over something neither can now remember exactly. One of them needs a favor.
A translator encounters a word they cannot render, and it is not a difficult word.
Memory can be donated like blood. Write about a person who has given too much.
A city votes each spring on which parts of its own history to keep. Write about the archivist who loses.
Faster-than-light travel exists, but only works for cargo nobody is waiting on. Write the shipping industry that results.
Every person is born knowing one true fact about a stranger they will never meet. Write about someone who finally meets theirs.
A generation ship's third generation votes on whether to wake the crew that launched it.
Write about the last human employee at a company that no longer requires humans, whose job is genuinely necessary.
Grief has been treatable as a disease for a decade. Write the first person to publicly refuse the cure.
An AI is asked to write the eulogy for its own creator, and gets one detail deliberately wrong.
Colonists discover their new world's seasons are eleven years long, and they arrived in spring.
Write about a repair technician for a technology nobody remembers the purpose of, which everyone still funds.
Something in the house has learned to imitate the sound of someone coming home.
A woman notices the family photographs are being replaced, one per week, with nearly identical versions.
Write about a small town where everyone is unfailingly kind, and it is getting worse.
A night watchman's rounds take fifty-two minutes. Tonight they take forty-nine.
Someone finds a door in their apartment that was always there, according to the lease, the landlord, and their partner.
Write about the thing that lives in the lake, from the perspective of the people who feed it, who are not afraid.
A child's imaginary friend has begun asking questions that suggest it is taking notes.
Every mirror in the building shows the room one second late.
Write about a support group where every member describes the same event, which none of them attended.
The neighbors' dog has not barked in six days, and the neighbors seem happier.
A locksmith is called to open a door and recognizes their own work from thirty years ago.
Write a detective who solves the case in the first ten minutes, and spends the rest of the story deciding whether to say so.
Every witness gives the same account, word for word, and none of them know each other.
A body is found with a train ticket to a station that closed in 1974.
Someone has been quietly correcting the errors on a small museum's placards for years. Write the curator who catches them.
Write about a missing person who has left a trail clearly meant to be followed, and clearly meant to take a long time.
An accountant finds a rounding error that has been running, deliberately, for two decades.
The security footage shows the room empty for four minutes. Everyone who was in it remembers those four minutes differently.
Write about the person who reports a crime that has not happened yet, and is right.
A letter arrives addressed to the house, not to anyone in it.
Write the minutes of a homeowners' association meeting that escalates into a schism.
A very serious professional must explain their job to a five-year-old who keeps asking why, and eventually cracks.
Two people who despise each other are stuck co-hosting a podcast that is finally succeeding.
A man has been faking a mild allergy for eight years and can no longer stop.
A cursed object is genuinely trying its best.
Write a customer service exchange in which the customer is completely correct and it changes nothing.
Someone's autocorrect has developed opinions about their relationship.
A bakery and a funeral home share a wall, a parking lot, and increasingly, a customer base.
Write the worst possible person to be trapped in an elevator with, from that person's point of view, in which they are lovely.
A small town's tourism board must rebrand around the only thing that has ever happened there.
Write a poem that is a list of everything you would have to explain to make one photograph make sense.
Write about winter light in a room, without naming the season, the light, or the room.
A poem whose last line is identical to its first, and has changed meaning.
Write about a body of water you know well as though describing a person's face.
Write a poem entirely in questions, none of which are rhetorical.
Take the most boring object within arm's reach. Write it as though it survived something.
Write about a hand doing work the person is no longer paying attention to.
A poem about a place that has been renamed, using only the old name's associations.
Write about leaving, in which nobody leaves.
Write a poem made of things overheard, arranged so that they argue.
First contact goes perfectly. Write the second contact.
A terraforming crew discovers the planet was terraformed once before, badly.
Write the engineer who has to explain that the mission cannot be sped up, to people who will die waiting.
A probe returns after two centuries carrying nothing it was sent for.
Write about the first person born off Earth who has no interest in ever visiting.
The signal repeats every eleven hours. It has been doing so since before there was anyone to hear it.
A ship's doctor must decide which specialist to wake, knowing the rest may never be.
Write about a species whose written language cannot express the future tense, and the diplomat assigned to them.
Gravity on the station has been off by two percent for a year and nobody reported it.
Write the last transmission from a colony that is completely fine.
A courier realizes the package they have carried across three districts is addressed to themselves.
Write about the last independent repair shop in a city where repair is illegal.
Someone's implant has begun showing ads only they can see, and one of them is correct.
A corporate arbitration clerk finds the clause that would free everyone, and it is three lines long.
Write about a street doctor who accepts payment only in favors, and is owed far too many.
The city's surveillance network has developed a preference for one particular citizen.
A woman sells the rights to her own face and watches it get worse.
Write the night shift at a data haven built inside a decommissioned grain elevator.
Someone is hired to forget something professionally, and the job goes well.
A gang war is settled entirely through competing service outages.
